title: Becoming a Knight
objective: After this level you can explain how a boy trained to become a knight.
summary: A noble boy served as a page from about 7, joined his father's lord's household at about 12, and trained as a squire before being dubbed with the accolade, if he could afford the equipment.

cards.headline: Becoming a knight could start at about the age of 7.
cards.body: Long before a sword touched his shoulder, a boy of noble birth spent years serving, learning and carrying other people’s gear. Here’s the road, step by step.

cards.headline: Step one: page
cards.body: A boy destined for knighthood might serve as a page from about the age of 7. At around 12 he joined the household of his father’s lord for further training. At this stage he might be called a damoiseau, literally “lordling”. Think of it as boarding school with horses, where the head teacher was your father’s lord.

cards.headline: Step two: squire
cards.body: Next he served as a squire: a young man of noble birth, apprenticed in the duties of chivalry, who looked after a knight’s armour and weapons. The training went well beyond fighting, taking in hunting, music and dancing. The goal was a worthy knight, a just master and a sensible manager of an estate. Swordplay, dance steps and estate accounts: a demanding timetable.

cards.headline: Step three: the accolade
cards.body: When he was skilled enough, and had the money, he was dubbed. The accolade was a touch on the shoulder with the flat of a sword blade. But he had to buy his own knightly equipment, and in France some squires waited for, or put off, the expensive dubbing. Many knights were vassals holding lands as fiefs from the lords they fought for. Remember Level 21’s land-for-service deal? These are the men who turned up.

questions.prompt: During a future knight’s training, a squire looked after _____.

options.label: the books in the lord’s chapel

questions.explanation: A squire was a young noble apprenticed in chivalry who attended to a knight’s armour and weapons.

questions.prompt: Put the steps to knighthood in order.
questions.explanation: A boy served as a page from about 7, might be called a damoiseau from around 12, then served as a squire, and finally received the accolade when he was dubbed.

questions.prompt: Medieval lords granted land in return for service. How did many knights fit that picture?

options.label: They were serfs bound to a plot
They were paid wages by the Church
They were given castles by the pope himself
They were vassals holding fiefs from lords

questions.explanation: Many knights were vassals holding lands as fiefs from the lords in whose armies they served.
